In fact, one may argue that the previous control approaches (i.e., chiller priori, TES priori, and constant proportion) may be a subcategory of RBCs [52]. Nonetheless, the development of RBCs requires prior knowledge of how the system will perform under different conditions [26], [35]. Advanced control strategies include optimal controllers and model predictive controllers (MPCs). MPCs are more sophisticated, as they are equipped with precise models to forecast future behavior over the next time horizons. These prediction models are then fed into an optimizer to determine the most suitable decision for the next time step. Such controls typically involve an optimizer that uses an objective function to read inputs such as ambient conditions, cost ratios, and plant system feedback, then determines how to operate the system to meet the objective function within the second requirement of the system's defined constraints. The objective function is a time-based function, and its simplest form is represented in Eq.(1), which is a minimization cost function [35]. Other forms of functions may exist, such as minimizing energy consumption [54] or maximizing COP. This objective function varies based on the system's user requirements [34].  n  J =min ∑cE +c max (E ) (1) i i peak 1≤i≤n peak   i=1 The last requirement is the optimizer solver, which can be either a mathematical or a metaheuristic solver. For mathematical optimizers that use numerical solvers such as Newton-Raphson, steepest descent, and so on, three approaches can be used: (i) mixed- integer linear programming, (ii) mixed integer non-linear programming, and (iii) dynamic programming, utilized in HP-TES system at [55], [56], [57], [58], [59], [60]. Heuristic optimizers that were investigated in the literature include genetic algorithms (GAs) and particle swarm optimizers (PSOs) [61], [62], [63]. Nonetheless, most of the defined advanced control techniques were presented in simulation-based environments using reduced-order models rather than in field tests, due to their complex applications.
